question: For the given uniform square lamina ABCD, whose centre is O, E and F are the midpoints of AB and DC. Then
diagram_alt: Square lamina ABCD with centre O, diagonal AC and line EF joining the midpoints of AB and DC
solution:
All axes here lie in the plane of the lamina and pass through O (except AD).

By the perpendicular axis theorem, for any two perpendicular in-plane axes through O: $I_1 + I_2 = I_z$ (the axis perpendicular to the plane).

EF and the line GH through O parallel to AB are perpendicular and, by symmetry, equal: $2I_{EF} = I_z$.

The diagonals AC and BD are also perpendicular and equal: $2I_{AC} = I_z$.

So $I_{AC} = I_{EF}$.

(For reference, $I_{AD} = I_{EF} + m\left(\dfrac{a}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{ma^2}{12} + \dfrac{ma^2}{4} = 4I_{EF}$.)
